name: Handle CIM request
info:
**Placeholder pass-through** between `Bridge to CIM` (in `Bridge entry to client`) and `POST to CIM`.

Add last-mile transformation of the outbound CIM payload here — set extra registration fields, build a primary_marker, customise subject/category — without touching the core POST pipeline.

### Input
`msg.payload` — CIM case-creation body produced by `Bridge to CIM`:

```js
{
  subject:       "[parat_bridge: <conn>] <author>",
  description:   "<bridge entry text>",
  source:        "Parat Bridge",
  reported_date: "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm"   // Norwegian local time
}
```

`msg.metadata` — entry metadata (`source`, `target`, `connection_name`).
`msg.entry`    — the canonical bridge entry the payload was built from (id, text, timestamp, author, files, labels, metadata).

### Output
Same shape. The body sent to CIM **must conform to the registration schema**:
- `additionalProperties: false` — only known schema keys allowed; CIM rejects unknown keys with HTTP 400
- Flat structure (no wrapper objects like `registration: {...}`)
- `subject` is required, 1–200 chars
- See `cim-api-findings.md` for the full schema (`source`, `description`, `category_text`, `cause`, `reported_date`, `org_id`, `responsible_id`, `primary_marker`, …)

### Safe extension pattern

The subflow ships as pure pass-through (no nodes between `in` and `out`). To add behaviour, **never** route every message through your logic — gate it with a switch so non-applicable messages bypass untouched:

```
[ in ] --> [ switch on condition ] --> branch 1: [ your logic ] --+
                                   --> branch 2 (otherwise): ----+--> [ out ]
```

Switch settings:
- `checkall: true`
- the last rule is `otherwise`, wired straight to the subflow `out`
- your branch ends at the same `out`

That way:
- matching messages get your transformation
- non-matching messages flow through with the default `Bridge to CIM` payload

### Things to avoid

- **Don't introduce keys outside the registration schema.** CIM strictly rejects unknown properties with HTTP 400. Allowed keys: `subject`, `status`, `source`, `description`, `category_text`, `cause`, `reported_date`, `case_created` (POST only), `org_id`, `location`, `responsible_id`, `user`, `primary_marker`. Anything else fails the request.
- **Don't mutate `msg.metadata.target.client_system`.** The upstream `POST entries` switch already routed on it; changing it here only confuses debugging.
- **Don't return `null` unless you intend to drop the message.** Returning null here cancels the POST silently (the queue entry will eventually retry and drop after MAX_RETRIES).
- **Don't put coordinates anywhere except `primary_marker`.** Lat/long must live inside `{ lat, long, markerName }` per the schema.

### Typical use cases

- Set `category_text`, `cause`, or `org_id` based on `msg.entry.labels` or `msg.metadata.source.client_system`
- Build `primary_marker` from coordinates parsed out of `entry.text`
- Append extra context to `subject` (with truncation — max 200 chars)
- Override `reported_date` formatting (still must be `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm` Norwegian local — use `utils.format_cim_timestamp`)
